3411 // Push onto stack
3412 struct IP_push: P {
3413  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3414  assert_args(insn, args, 1);
3415  if (insn->get_lockPrefix()) {
3416  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
3417  } else {
3418  // Stack pointer register
3419  RegisterDescriptor sp;
3420  switch (insn->get_addressSize()) {
3421  case x86_insnsize_16: sp = d->REG_SP; break;
3422  case x86_insnsize_32: sp = d->REG_ESP; break;
3423  case x86_insnsize_64: sp = d->REG_RSP; break;
3424  default:
3425  ASSERT_not_reachable("invalid address size");
3426  }
3427  ASSERT_forbid(sp.isEmpty());
3428 
3429  // Read the value to push onto the stack before decrementing the stack pointer.
3430  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr toPush = d->read(args[0]);
3431  if (isSgAsmIntegerValueExpression(args[0]) && toPush->nBits() < sp.nBits()) {
3432  toPush = ops->signExtend(toPush, sp.nBits());
3433  } else if (isSgAsmRegisterReferenceExpression(args[0]) && toPush->nBits() < sp.nBits() &&
3434  (isSgAsmRegisterReferenceExpression(args[0])->get_descriptor() == d->REG_FS ||
3435  isSgAsmRegisterReferenceExpression(args[0])->get_descriptor() == d->REG_GS)) {
3436  toPush = ops->unsignedExtend(toPush, sp.nBits());
3437  }
3438 
3439  // Decrement the stack pointer before writing to args[0] just in case args[0] is stack-relative
3440  int stackDelta = toPush->nBits() / 8;
3441  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr oldSp = d->readRegister(sp);
3442  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr newSp = ops->add(oldSp, ops->number_(sp.nBits(), -stackDelta));
3443  d->writeRegister(sp, newSp);
3444 
3445  // Write data to stack
3446  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr addr = d->fixMemoryAddress(newSp);
3447  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, addr, toPush, ops->boolean_(true));
3448  }
3449  }
3450 };
3451 
3452 // Push all general-purpose registers
3453 struct IP_push_gprs: P {
3454  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3455  assert_args(insn, args, 0);
3456  if (insn->get_lockPrefix()) {
3457  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
3458  } else if (insn->get_addressSize() == x86_insnsize_16) {
3459  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr oldSp = d->readRegister(d->REG_anySP);
3460  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr newSp = ops->add(oldSp, ops->number_(oldSp->nBits(), -16));
3461  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr base = d->fixMemoryAddress(newSp);
3462  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr yes = ops->boolean_(true);
3463  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr di = d->readRegister(d->REG_DI);
3464  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, base, di, yes);
3465  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr si = d->readRegister(d->REG_SI);
3466  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, ops->add(base, ops->number_(base->nBits(), 2)), si, yes);
3467  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr bp = d->readRegister(d->REG_BP);
3468  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, ops->add(base, ops->number_(base->nBits(), 4)), bp, yes);
3469  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, ops->add(base, ops->number_(base->nBits(), 6)), oldSp, yes);
3470  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr bx = d->readRegister(d->REG_BX);
3471  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, ops->add(base, ops->number_(base->nBits(), 8)), bx, yes);
3472  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr dx = d->readRegister(d->REG_DX);
3473  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, ops->add(base, ops->number_(base->nBits(), 10)), dx, yes);
3474  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr cx = d->readRegister(d->REG_CX);
3475  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, ops->add(base, ops->number_(base->nBits(), 12)), cx, yes);
3476  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr ax = d->readRegister(d->REG_AX);
3477  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, ops->add(base, ops->number_(base->nBits(), 14)), ax, yes);
3478  d->writeRegister(d->REG_anySP, newSp);
3479  } else if (insn->get_addressSize() == x86_insnsize_32) {
3480  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr oldSp = d->readRegister(d->REG_anySP);
3481  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr newSp = ops->add(oldSp, ops->number_(oldSp->nBits(), -32));
3482  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr base = d->fixMemoryAddress(newSp);
3483  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr yes = ops->boolean_(true);
3484  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr edi = d->readRegister(d->REG_EDI);
3485  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, base, edi, yes);
3486  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr esi = d->readRegister(d->REG_ESI);
3487  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, ops->add(base, ops->number_(base->nBits(), 4)), esi, yes);
3488  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr ebp = d->readRegister(d->REG_EBP);
3489  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, ops->add(base, ops->number_(base->nBits(), 8)), ebp, yes);
3490  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, ops->add(base, ops->number_(base->nBits(), 12)), oldSp, yes);
3491  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr ebx = d->readRegister(d->REG_EBX);
3492  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, ops->add(base, ops->number_(base->nBits(), 16)), ebx, yes);
3493  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr edx = d->readRegister(d->REG_EDX);
3494  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, ops->add(base, ops->number_(base->nBits(), 20)), edx, yes);
3495  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr ecx = d->readRegister(d->REG_ECX);
3496  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, ops->add(base, ops->number_(base->nBits(), 24)), ecx, yes);
3497  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr eax = d->readRegister(d->REG_EAX);
3498  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, ops->add(base, ops->number_(base->nBits(), 28)), eax, yes);
3499  d->writeRegister(d->REG_anySP, newSp);
3500  } else {
3501  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0); // 64-bit mode
3502  }
3503  }
3504 };

3506 // Push EFLAGS onto the stack
3507 struct IP_push_flags: P {
3508  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3509  assert_args(insn, args, 0);
3510  if (insn->get_lockPrefix()) {
3511  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
3512  } else {
3513  // Get the value to be pushed. Assume non-priviledged.
3514  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr flags;
3515  switch (insn->get_operandSize()) {
3516  case x86_insnsize_16:
3517  flags = d->readRegister(d->REG_FLAGS);
3518  break;
3519  case x86_insnsize_32:
3520  flags = d->readRegister(d->REG_EFLAGS);
3521  break;
3522  case x86_insnsize_64:
3523  flags = d->readRegister(d->REG_RFLAGS);
3524  break;
3525  default:
3526  ASSERT_not_reachable("invalid operand size");
3527  }
3528 
3529  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr valueToPush = ops->extract(flags, 0, 16);
3530  if (flags->nBits() >= 32) {
3531  valueToPush = ops->concat(valueToPush, ops->number_(2, 0)); // clear VM and RF, bits 16 and 17
3532  valueToPush = ops->concat(valueToPush, ops->extract(flags, 18, 32));
3533  if (flags->nBits() == 64)
3534  valueToPush = ops->concat(valueToPush, ops->extract(flags, 32, 64));
3535  }
3536 
3537  // Push value onto stack
3538  ASSERT_not_null(valueToPush);
3539  ASSERT_require(valueToPush->nBits() % 8 == 0);
3540  size_t valueSize = valueToPush->nBits() / 8;
3541  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr oldSp = d->readRegister(d->REG_anySP);
3542  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr newSp = ops->add(oldSp, ops->number_(oldSp->nBits(), -valueSize));
3543  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr addr = d->fixMemoryAddress(newSp);
3544  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_SS, addr, valueToPush, ops->boolean_(true));
3545  d->writeRegister(d->REG_anySP, newSp);
3546  }
3547  }
3548 };
3549 
3550 // Bitwise XOR
3551 struct IP_pxor: P {
3552  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3553  assert_args(insn, args, 2);
3554  size_t nbits = asm_type_width(args[0]->get_type());
3555  if (nbits!=asm_type_width(args[1]->get_type()))
3556  throw BaseSemantics::Exception("PXOR operands must be the same width", insn);
3557  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr result;
3558 
3559  // XOR of a register with itself is an x86 idiom for setting the register to zero, so treat it as such
3560  if (isSgAsmRegisterReferenceExpression(args[0]) && isSgAsmRegisterReferenceExpression(args[1])) {
3561  RegisterDescriptor r1 = isSgAsmRegisterReferenceExpression(args[0])->get_descriptor();
3562  RegisterDescriptor r2 = isSgAsmRegisterReferenceExpression(args[1])->get_descriptor();
3563  if (r1==r2)
3564  result = ops->number_(nbits, 0);
3565  }
3566 
3567  // The non-idiomatic behavior
3568  if (result==NULL) {
3569  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr arg1 = d->read(args[1], nbits);
3570  result = ops->xor_(d->read(args[0], nbits), arg1);
3571  }
3572 
3573  d->write(args[0], result);
3574  }
3575 };
3576 
3577 // Return from procedure
3578 struct IP_ret: P {
3579  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3580  if (args.size()>1)
3581  throw BaseSemantics::Exception("instruction must have zero or one operand", insn);
3582  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr oldSp = d->readRegister(d->REG_anySP);
3583  size_t stackDelta = d->REG_anyIP.nBits() / 8;
3584  if (args.size() == 1) {
3585  ASSERT_require(isSgAsmIntegerValueExpression(args[0]));
3586  stackDelta += isSgAsmIntegerValueExpression(args[0])->get_absoluteValue();
3587  }
3588  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr newSp = ops->add(oldSp, ops->number_(oldSp->nBits(), stackDelta));
3589  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr stackVa = d->fixMemoryAddress(oldSp);
3590  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr yes = ops->boolean_(true);
3591  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr retVa = ops->filterReturnTarget(ops->readMemory(d->REG_SS, stackVa,
3592  ops->undefined_(d->REG_anyIP.nBits()),
3593  yes));
3594  d->writeRegister(d->REG_anyIP, retVa);
3595  d->writeRegister(d->REG_anySP, newSp);
3596  }
3597 };

3599 // Various rotate instructions. Handles RCL, RCR, ROL, and ROR for 8, 16, 32, and 64 bits
3600 struct IP_rotate: P {
3601  const X86InstructionKind kind;
3602  const bool with_cf;
3603  IP_rotate(X86InstructionKind k): kind(k), with_cf(x86_rcl==kind || x86_rcr==kind) {
3604  ASSERT_require(x86_rcl==k || x86_rcr==k || x86_rol==k || x86_ror==k);
3605  }
3606  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3607  assert_args(insn, args, 2);
3608  ASSERT_require(insn->get_kind()==kind);
3609  if (insn->get_lockPrefix()) {
3610  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
3611  } else {
3612  size_t nbits = asm_type_width(args[0]->get_type());
3613  // FIXME: Intel documentation contains conflicting statements about the number of significant bits in the rotate
3614  // count. We're doing what seems most reasonable: 6-bit counts for any operand (inc. CF) that's wider than 32
3615  // bits.
3616  size_t rotateWidth = (nbits>32 || (32==nbits && with_cf)) ? 6 : 5;
3617  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr operand = d->read(args[0]);
3618  if (with_cf)
3619  operand = ops->concat(operand, d->readRegister(d->REG_CF));
3620  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr rotateCount = d->read(args[1], 8);
3621  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr result = d->doRotateOperation(kind, operand, rotateCount, rotateWidth);
3622  // flags have been updated; we just need to store the result
3623  if (with_cf)
3624  result = ops->extract(result, 0, nbits);
3625  d->write(args[0], result);
3626  }
3627  }
3628 };

3630 // Integer subtraction with borrow
3631 struct IP_sbb: P {
3632  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3633  assert_args(insn, args, 2);
3634  if (insn->get_lockPrefix() && !isSgAsmMemoryReferenceExpression(args[0])) {
3635  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
3636  } else {
3637  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr minuend = d->read(args[0]);
3638  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr subtrahend = d->read(args[1]);
3639  if (minuend->nBits() > subtrahend->nBits())
3640  subtrahend = ops->signExtend(subtrahend, minuend->nBits());
3641  ASSERT_require(minuend->nBits() == subtrahend->nBits());
3642  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr cf = d->readRegister(d->REG_CF);
3643  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr difference = d->doAddOperation(minuend, ops->invert(subtrahend), true, cf);
3644  d->write(args[0], difference);
3645  }
3646  }
3647 };

3649 // Scan string
3650 // The disassembler produces SCASB, SCASW, SCASD, or SCASQ without any arguments (never SCAS with an arg)
3651 struct IP_scanstring: P {
3652  const X86RepeatPrefix repeat;
3653  const size_t nbits;
3654  const size_t nbytes;
3655  IP_scanstring(X86RepeatPrefix repeat, size_t nbits): repeat(repeat), nbits(nbits), nbytes(nbits/8) {
3656  ASSERT_require(8==nbits || 16==nbits || 32==nbits || 64==nbits);
3657  }
3658  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3659  assert_args(insn, args, 0);
3660  if (insn->get_lockPrefix()) {
3661  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
3662  } else {
3663  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr inLoop = d->repEnter(repeat);
3664 
3665  // Get the address for the string
3666  RegisterDescriptor stringReg;
3667  switch (insn->get_addressSize()) {
3668  case x86_insnsize_16:
3669  stringReg = d->REG_DI;
3670  break;
3671  case x86_insnsize_32:
3672  stringReg = d->REG_EDI;
3673  break;
3674  case x86_insnsize_64:
3675  stringReg = d->REG_RDI;
3676  break;
3677  default:
3678  ASSERT_not_reachable("invalid instruction address size");
3679  }
3680  ASSERT_forbid(stringReg.isEmpty());
3681  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr stringPtr = d->readRegister(stringReg);
3682 
3683  // Adjust address width based on how memory is accessed. All addresses in memory have the same width.
3684  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr addr = d->fixMemoryAddress(stringPtr);
3685 
3686  // Compare values and set status flags.
3687  RegisterDescriptor compareReg = d->REG_AX; compareReg.nBits(nbits);
3688  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr val1 = d->readRegister(compareReg);
3689  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr val2 = ops->readMemory(d->REG_ES, addr, ops->undefined_(nbits), inLoop);
3690  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr no = ops->boolean_(false);
3691  (void) d->doAddOperation(val1, ops->invert(val2), true, no, inLoop);
3692 
3693  // Advance string pointer register
3694  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr positiveNBytes = ops->number_(stringReg.nBits(), +nbytes);
3695  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr negativeNBytes = ops->number_(stringReg.nBits(), -nbytes);
3696  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr step = ops->ite(d->readRegister(d->REG_DF), negativeNBytes, positiveNBytes);
3697  d->writeRegister(stringReg, ops->ite(inLoop, ops->add(stringPtr, step), stringPtr));
3698 
3699  // Adjust the instruction pointer register to either repeat the instruction or fall through
3700  if (x86_repeat_none != repeat)
3701  d->repLeave(repeat, inLoop, insn->get_address(), true/*use ZF*/);
3702  }
3703  }
3704 };
3705 
3706 // Set byte on condition
3707 struct IP_setcc: P {
3708  const X86InstructionKind kind;
3709  IP_setcc(X86InstructionKind k): kind(k) {
3710  ASSERT_require(x86_setne==k || x86_sete==k || x86_setno==k || x86_seto==k || x86_setpo==k || x86_setpe==k ||
3711  x86_setns==k || x86_sets==k || x86_setae==k || x86_setb==k || x86_setbe==k || x86_seta==k ||
3712  x86_setle==k || x86_setg==k || x86_setge==k || x86_setl==k);
3713  }
3714  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3715  assert_args(insn, args, 1);
3716  ASSERT_require(insn->get_kind()==kind);
3717  if (insn->get_lockPrefix()) {
3718  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
3719  } else {
3720  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr cond = d->flagsCombo(kind);
3721  d->write(args[0], ops->concat(cond, ops->number_(7, 0)));

3726 // Shift instructions: SHL, SAR, and SHR
3727 struct IP_shift_1: P {
3728  const X86InstructionKind kind;
3729  IP_shift_1(X86InstructionKind k): kind(k) {
3730  ASSERT_require(x86_shr==k || x86_sar==k || x86_shl==k);
3731  }
3732  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3733  assert_args(insn, args, 2);
3734  ASSERT_require(insn->get_kind()==kind);
3735  if (insn->get_lockPrefix()) {
3736  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
3737  } else {
3738  size_t nbits = asm_type_width(args[0]->get_type());
3739  size_t shiftSignificantBits = nbits <= 32 ? 5 : 6;
3740  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr arg1 = d->read(args[1], 8);
3741  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr unspecified = ops->unspecified_(nbits);
3742  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr result = d->doShiftOperation(kind, d->read(args[0]), unspecified,
3743  arg1, shiftSignificantBits);
3744  d->write(args[0], result);
3745  }

3749 // Double-wide shift: SHLD
3750 struct IP_shift_2: P {

3752  IP_shift_2(X86InstructionKind k): kind(k) {
3753  ASSERT_require(x86_shld==k || x86_shrd==k);
3754  }
3755  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3756  assert_args(insn, args, 3);
3757  ASSERT_require(insn->get_kind()==kind);
3758  if (insn->get_lockPrefix()) {
3759  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
3760  } else {
3761  size_t halfWidth = asm_type_width(args[0]->get_type());
3762  size_t shiftSignificantBits = halfWidth <= 32 ? 5 : 6;
3763  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr arg2 = d->read(args[2], 8);
3764  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr arg1 = d->read(args[1]);
3765  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr result = d->doShiftOperation(kind, d->read(args[0]), arg1, arg2, shiftSignificantBits);
3766  d->write(args[0], result);
3767  }
3768  }

3795 // Store string
3796 // The disassembler produces STOSB, STOSW, STOSD, or STOSQ without any arguments (never STOS with an arg)
3797 struct IP_storestring: P {
3798  const X86RepeatPrefix repeat;
3799  const size_t nbits;
3800  const size_t nbytes;
3801  IP_storestring(X86RepeatPrefix repeat, size_t nbits): repeat(repeat), nbits(nbits), nbytes(nbits/8) {
3802  ASSERT_require(8==nbits || 16==nbits || 32==nbits || 64==nbits);
3803  }
3804  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3805  assert_args(insn, args, 0);
3806  if (insn->get_lockPrefix()) {
3807  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
3808  } else {
3809  // Get the address for storing.
3810  RegisterDescriptor dstReg;
3811  switch (insn->get_addressSize()) {
3812  case x86_insnsize_16:
3813  dstReg = d->REG_DI;
3814  break;
3815  case x86_insnsize_32:
3816  dstReg = d->REG_EDI;
3817  break;
3818  case x86_insnsize_64:
3819  dstReg = d->REG_RDI;
3820  break;
3821  default:
3822  ASSERT_not_reachable("invalid instruction address size");
3823  }
3824  ASSERT_forbid(dstReg.isEmpty());
3825  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr stringPtr = d->readRegister(dstReg);
3826  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr addr = d->fixMemoryAddress(stringPtr);
3827  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr directionFlag = d->readRegister(d->REG_DF);
3828  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr positiveNBytes = ops->number_(dstReg.nBits(), +nbytes);
3829  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr step = ops->ite(directionFlag,
3830  ops->number_(dstReg.nBits(), -nbytes),
3831  positiveNBytes);
3832 
3833  // Source value
3834  RegisterDescriptor regA = d->REG_AX; regA.nBits(nbits);
3835  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr src = d->readRegister(regA);
3836 
3837  // If CX is a known value then we can unroll the loop right now.
3838  if (x86_repeat_repe==repeat) {
3839  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr cx = d->readRegister(d->REG_anyCX);
3840  if (cx->toUnsigned().orElse(8192+1) <= 8192 /*arbitrary*/) {
3841  size_t n = cx->toUnsigned().get();
3842  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr inLoop = ops->boolean_(true);
3843  for (size_t i=0; i<n; ++i) {
3844  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr va =
3845  ops->add(addr,
3846  ops->unsignedExtend(ops->unsignedMultiply(ops->number_(addr->nBits(), i), step),
3847  addr->nBits()));
3848  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_ES, va, src, inLoop);
3849  }
3850  d->writeRegister(d->REG_anyCX, ops->number_(d->REG_anyCX.nBits(), 0));
3851 
3852  // Final value for (E)DI register
3853  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr va =
3854  ops->add(addr,
3855  ops->unsignedExtend(ops->unsignedMultiply(ops->number_(addr->nBits(), n), step),
3856  addr->nBits()));
3857  d->writeRegister(dstReg, va);
3858  return;
3859  }
3860  }
3861 
3862  // We chose not to unroll the loop, so simulate the loop by manipulating the instruction pointer
3863  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr inLoop = d->repEnter(repeat);
3864 
3865  // Copy value from AL/AX/EAX/RAX to memory
3866  ops->writeMemory(d->REG_ES, addr, src, inLoop);
3867 
3868  // Advance pointer register
3869  d->writeRegister(dstReg, ops->ite(inLoop, ops->add(stringPtr, step), stringPtr));
3870 
3871  // Adjust the instruction pointer register to either repeat the instruction or fall through
3872  if (x86_repeat_none != repeat)
3873  d->repLeave(repeat, inLoop, insn->get_address(), false/*no ZF*/);
3874  }
3875  }
3876 };
3877

3900  if (minuend->nBits() > subtrahend->nBits())
3901  subtrahend = ops->signExtend(subtrahend, minuend->nBits());

3933 
3934 // Same as x86_and except doesn't write result back to machine state
3935 struct IP_test: P {
3936  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3937  assert_args(insn, args, 2);
3938  if (insn->get_lockPrefix()) {
3939  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
3940  } else {
3941  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr a = d->read(args[0]);
3942  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr b = d->read(args[1]);
3943  if (a->nBits() > b->nBits())
3944  b = ops->signExtend(b, a->nBits());
3945  ASSERT_require(a->nBits() == b->nBits());
3946  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr result = ops->and_(a, b);
3947  d->setFlagsForResult(result);
3948  d->writeRegister(d->REG_OF, ops->boolean_(false));
3949  d->writeRegister(d->REG_AF, ops->unspecified_(1));
3950  d->writeRegister(d->REG_CF, ops->boolean_(false));
3951  }
3952  }
3953 };
3954 
3955 // Undefined instruction: UD2
3956 struct IP_ud2: P {
3957  void p(D, Ops ops, I, A) {
3958  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
3959  }
3960 };
3961 
3962 // Wait (check for and handle unmasked floating-point exceptions)
3963 struct IP_wait: P {
3964  void p(D, Ops, I insn, A args) {
3965  // FIXME[Robb P. Matzke 2014-05-12]: currenty a no-op
3966  assert_args(insn, args, 0);
3967  }
3968 };
3969 
3970 // Exchange and add
3971 struct IP_xadd: P {
3972  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3973  assert_args(insn, args, 2);
3974  if (insn->get_lockPrefix() &&
3975  !isSgAsmMemoryReferenceExpression(args[0]) && !isSgAsmMemoryReferenceExpression(args[1])) {
3976  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
3977  } else {
3978  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr no = ops->boolean_(false);
3979  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr arg1 = d->read(args[1]);
3980  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr sum = d->doAddOperation(d->read(args[0]), arg1, false, no);
3981  d->write(args[1], d->read(args[0]));
3982  d->write(args[0], sum);
3983  }
3984  }
3985 };
3986 
3987 // Exchange
3988 struct IP_xchg: P {
3989  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
3990  assert_args(insn, args, 2);
3991  if (insn->get_lockPrefix() &&
3992  !isSgAsmMemoryReferenceExpression(args[0]) && !isSgAsmMemoryReferenceExpression(args[1])) {
3993  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
3994  } else {
3995  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr temp = d->read(args[0]);
3996  d->write(args[0], d->read(args[1]));
3997  d->write(args[1], temp);
3998  }
3999  }
4000 };
4001 
4002 // Bitwise XOR
4003 // XOR
4004 // XORPD
4005 // XORPS
4006 struct IP_xor: P {
4007  void p(D d, Ops ops, I insn, A args) {
4008  assert_args(insn, args, 2);
4009  if (insn->get_lockPrefix() && !isSgAsmMemoryReferenceExpression(args[0])) {
4010  ops->interrupt(x86_exception_ud, 0);
4011  } else {
4012  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr result;
4013 
4014  if (isSgAsmDirectRegisterExpression(args[0]) && isSgAsmDirectRegisterExpression(args[1]) &&
4015  (isSgAsmRegisterReferenceExpression(args[0])->get_descriptor() ==
4016  isSgAsmRegisterReferenceExpression(args[1])->get_descriptor())) {
4017  // XOR of a register with itself is an x86 idiom for setting the register to zero, so treat it as such
4018  size_t nbits = asm_type_width(args[0]->get_type());
4019  result = ops->number_(nbits, 0);
4020  } else {
4021  // The non-idiomatic behavior
4022  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr a = d->read(args[0]);
4023  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr b = d->read(args[1]);
4024  if (a->nBits() > b->nBits())
4025  b = ops->signExtend(b, a->nBits());
4026  ASSERT_require(a->nBits() == b->nBits());
4027  result = ops->xor_(a, b);
4028  }
4029 
4030  d->setFlagsForResult(result);
4031  d->write(args[0], result);
4032  d->writeRegister(d->REG_OF, ops->boolean_(false));
4033  d->writeRegister(d->REG_AF, ops->unspecified_(1));
4034  d->writeRegister(d->REG_CF, ops->boolean_(false));
4035  }
4036  }
4037 };
4038 
4039 } // namespace

4455  REG_R12 = findRegister("r12", 64);

4460  case x86_insnsize_32:
4461  REG_EAX = findRegister("eax", 32);

4473  REG_GS = findRegister("gs", 16);
4474  // fall through...
4475  case x86_insnsize_16:
4476  REG_AX = findRegister("ax", 16);

4479  REG_DX = findRegister("dx", 16);

4488  REG_DL = findRegister("dl", 8);
4489  REG_AH = findRegister("ah", 8);
4490  REG_BH = findRegister("bh", 8);
4491  REG_CH = findRegister("ch", 8);
4492  REG_DH = findRegister("dh", 8);
4493  REG_FLAGS = findRegister("flags", 16);
4494  REG_AF = findRegister("af", 1);
4495  REG_CF = findRegister("cf", 1);
4496  REG_DF = findRegister("df", 1);
4497  REG_OF = findRegister("of", 1);
4498  REG_PF = findRegister("pf", 1);
4499  REG_SF = findRegister("sf", 1);
4500  REG_TF = findRegister("tf", 1);
4501  REG_ZF = findRegister("zf", 1);
4502  REG_CS = findRegister("cs", 16);
4503  REG_DS = findRegister("ds", 16);
4504  REG_ES = findRegister("es", 16);
4505  REG_SS = findRegister("ss", 16);
4506 
4507  // These next few are not in every 16-bit architecture
4508  REG_FPSTATUS = findRegister("fpstatus", 16, true);

4512  break;
4513  default:
4514  ASSERT_not_reachable("invalid instruction size");
4515  }
4516 
4517  size_t maxWidth = 0;

4520  case x86_insnsize_32: maxWidth = 32; break;

4524 
4525  RegisterDictionary::Ptr regdict = architecture()->registerDictionary();
4526 
4527  REG_anyAX = regdict->findLargestRegister(x86_regclass_gpr, x86_gpr_ax, maxWidth);

4542 void
4543 DispatcherX86::initializeState(const BaseSemantics::State::Ptr &state) {
4544  if (state) {
4545  // Back in the 16-bit days, segment registers were actually used to increase the amount of memory that could be
4546  // addressed since addresses where only 16-bits.
4547  //
4548  // Then when 32-bit processors came along there was no real need for segment registers, but they were kept in the
4549  // architecture for backwards-compatibility. Conventionally, CS, DS, SS, and ES were all set to zero in Windows and FS
4550  // was an offset in low memory to a process' thread environment block. Something similar happened in Linux. GS wasn't
4551  // used for anything initially (zero in practice), and eventually got used for some other features in GCC. It may still
4552  // be unused (zero) in Windows generally. It appears that there are no official declarations from Intel on how these
4553  // registers are to be used in this era.
4554  //
4555  // Then with 64-bit processors, Intel's guidance became a lot clearer. The Intel manual on Volume 1, Section 3.3.4
4556  // "Modes of Operation vs. Memory Model" page Vol 1 3-9 reads "Segmentation is generally (but not completely) disabled,
4557  // creating a flat 64-bit linear-address space. The processor treats the segment base of CS, DS, ES, and SS as zero,
4558  // creating a linear address that is equal to the effective address. The exceptions are the FS and GS segments, whose
4559  // segment registers (which hold the segment base) can be used as additional base registers in some linear address
4560  // calculations.
4561  //
4562  // Therefore, ROSE initializes CS, DS, SS, and ES to zero and it's up to the caller to modify these registers if
4563  // setting them to zero is not appropriate. Also, note that for simplicity, ROSE treates the segment registers as
4564  // memory offsets rather than indexes into a descriptor table.
4565  ASSERT_not_null(operators());
4566  state->writeRegister(REG_CS, operators()->number_(REG_CS.nBits(), 0), operators().get());
4567  state->writeRegister(REG_DS, operators()->number_(REG_DS.nBits(), 0), operators().get());
4568  state->writeRegister(REG_SS, operators()->number_(REG_SS.nBits(), 0), operators().get());
4569  state->writeRegister(REG_ES, operators()->number_(REG_ES.nBits(), 0), operators().get());
4570  }
4571 }
4572 
4573 void
4574 DispatcherX86::memory_init() {
4575  if (BaseSemantics::State::Ptr state = currentState()) {
4576  if (BaseSemantics::MemoryState::Ptr memory = state->memoryState()) {
4577  switch (memory->get_byteOrder()) {
4578  case ByteOrder::ORDER_LSB:
4579  break;
4580  case ByteOrder::ORDER_MSB:
4581  mlog[WARN] <<"x86 memory state is using big-endian byte order\n";
4582  break;
4583  case ByteOrder::ORDER_UNSPECIFIED:
4584  memory->set_byteOrder(ByteOrder::ORDER_LSB);
4585  break;
4586  }
4587  }
4588  }
4589 }

4606 static bool
4607 isStatusRegister(RegisterDescriptor reg) {
4608  return reg.majorNumber()==x86_regclass_flags && reg.minorNumber()==x86_flags_status;

4611 RegisterDictionary::RegisterDescriptors
4612 DispatcherX86::get_usual_registers() const
4613 {
4614  RegisterDictionary::Ptr regdict = architecture()->registerDictionary();
4615  RegisterDictionary::RegisterDescriptors registers = regdict->getLargestRegisters();
4616  registers.erase(std::remove_if(registers.begin(), registers.end(), isStatusRegister), registers.end());
4617  for (RegisterDescriptor reg: regdict->getSmallestRegisters()) {
4618  if (isStatusRegister(reg))
4619  registers.push_back(reg);
4620  }
4621  return registers;
4622 }

4624 void
4625 DispatcherX86::setFlagsForResult(const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &result)
4626 {
4627  size_t width = result->nBits();
4628  writeRegister(REG_PF, parity(operators()->extract(result, 0, 8)));
4629  writeRegister(REG_SF, operators()->extract(result, width-1, width));
4630  writeRegister(REG_ZF, operators()->equalToZero(result));
4631 }
4632 
4633 void
4634 DispatcherX86::setFlagsForResult(const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &result, const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &cond)
4635 {
4636  ASSERT_require(cond->nBits()==1);
4637  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr lo_byte = operators()->extract(result, 0, 8);
4638  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr signbit = operators()->extract(result, result->nBits()-1, result->nBits());
4639  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr pf = readRegister(REG_PF, PEEK_REGISTER);
4640  writeRegister(REG_PF, operators()->ite(cond, parity(lo_byte), pf));
4641  writeRegister(REG_SF, operators()->ite(cond, signbit, readRegister(REG_SF, PEEK_REGISTER)));
4642  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr zf = readRegister(REG_ZF, PEEK_REGISTER);
4643  writeRegister(REG_ZF, operators()->ite(cond, operators()->equalToZero(result), zf));
4644 }
4645 
4646 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
4647 DispatcherX86::parity(const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &v)
4648 {
4649  ASSERT_require(v->nBits()==8);
4650  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr p1 = operators()->extract(v, 1, 2);
4651  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr p01 = operators()->xor_(operators()->extract(v, 0, 1), p1);
4652  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr p3 = operators()->extract(v, 3, 4);
4653  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr p23 = operators()->xor_(operators()->extract(v, 2, 3), p3);
4654  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr p5 = operators()->extract(v, 5, 6);
4655  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr p45 = operators()->xor_(operators()->extract(v, 4, 5), p5);
4656  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr p7 = operators()->extract(v, 7, 8);
4657  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr p67 = operators()->xor_(operators()->extract(v, 6, 7), p7);
4658  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr p0123 = operators()->xor_(p01, p23);
4659  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr p4567 = operators()->xor_(p45, p67);
4660  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr pall = operators()->xor_(p0123, p4567);
4661  return operators()->invert(pall);
4662 }

4664 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
4665 DispatcherX86::invertMaybe(const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &value, bool maybe)
4666 {
4667  return maybe ? operators()->invert(value) : value;
4668 }

4670 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
4671 DispatcherX86::greaterOrEqualToTen(const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &w)
4672 {
4673  size_t nbits = w->nBits();
4674  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr carries;
4675  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr no = operators()->boolean_(false);
4676  operators()->addWithCarries(w, number_(nbits, 6), no, carries/*out*/);
4677  return operators()->extract(carries, nbits-1, nbits);
4678 }

4680 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
4681 DispatcherX86::flagsCombo(X86InstructionKind k)
4682 {
4683  switch (k) {
4684  case x86_jne:
4685  case x86_setne:
4686  case x86_cmovne:
4687  return operators()->invert(readRegister(REG_ZF));
4688  case x86_je:
4689  case x86_sete:
4690  case x86_cmove:
4691  return readRegister(REG_ZF);
4692  case x86_jno:
4693  case x86_setno:
4694  case x86_cmovno:
4695  return operators()->invert(readRegister(REG_OF));
4696  case x86_jo:
4697  case x86_seto:
4698  case x86_cmovo:
4699  return readRegister(REG_OF);
4700  case x86_jns:
4701  case x86_setns:
4702  case x86_cmovns:
4703  return operators()->invert(readRegister(REG_SF));
4704  case x86_js:
4705  case x86_sets:
4706  case x86_cmovs:
4707  return readRegister(REG_SF);
4708  case x86_jpo:
4709  case x86_setpo:
4710  case x86_cmovpo:
4711  return operators()->invert(readRegister(REG_PF));
4712  case x86_jpe:
4713  case x86_setpe:
4714  case x86_cmovpe:
4715  return readRegister(REG_PF);
4716  case x86_jae:
4717  case x86_setae:
4718  case x86_cmovae:
4719  return operators()->invert(readRegister(REG_CF));
4720  case x86_jb:
4721  case x86_setb:
4722  case x86_cmovb:
4723  return readRegister(REG_CF);
4724  case x86_jbe:
4725  case x86_setbe:
4726  case x86_cmovbe: {
4727  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr zf = readRegister(REG_ZF);
4728  return operators()->or_(readRegister(REG_CF), zf);
4729  }
4730  case x86_ja:
4731  case x86_seta:
4732  case x86_cmova: {
4733  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr notZf = operators()->invert(readRegister(REG_ZF));
4734  return operators()->and_(operators()->invert(readRegister(REG_CF)), notZf);
4735  }
4736  case x86_jl:
4737  case x86_setl:
4738  case x86_cmovl: {
4739  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr of = readRegister(REG_OF);
4740  return operators()->xor_(readRegister(REG_SF), of);
4741  }
4742  case x86_jge:
4743  case x86_setge:
4744  case x86_cmovge: {
4745  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr of = readRegister(REG_OF);
4746  return operators()->invert(operators()->xor_(readRegister(REG_SF), of));
4747  }
4748  case x86_jle:
4749  case x86_setle:
4750  case x86_cmovle: {
4751  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr of = readRegister(REG_OF);
4752  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr sf_xor_of = operators()->xor_(readRegister(REG_SF), of);
4753  return operators()->or_(readRegister(REG_ZF), sf_xor_of);
4754  }
4755  case x86_jg:
4756  case x86_setg:
4757  case x86_cmovg: {
4758  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr notZf = operators()->invert(readRegister(REG_ZF));
4759  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr of = readRegister(REG_OF);
4760  return operators()->and_(operators()->invert(operators()->xor_(readRegister(REG_SF), of)), notZf);
4761  }
4762  case x86_jcxz:
4763  return operators()->equalToZero(readRegister(REG_CX));
4764  case x86_jecxz:
4765  return operators()->equalToZero(readRegister(REG_ECX));
4766  default:
4767  ASSERT_not_reachable("instruction kind not handled");
4768  }
4769 }

4771 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
4772 DispatcherX86::repEnter(X86RepeatPrefix repeat)
4773 {
4774  if (repeat==x86_repeat_none)
4775  return operators()->boolean_(true);
4776  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr cx = readRegister(REG_anyCX);
4777  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr in_loop = operators()->invert(operators()->equalToZero(cx));
4778  return in_loop;
4779 }
4780 
4781 void
4782 DispatcherX86::repLeave(X86RepeatPrefix repeat_prefix, const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &in_loop, Address insn_va,
4783  bool honorZeroFlag)
4784 {
4785  ASSERT_require(in_loop!=NULL && in_loop->nBits()==1);
4786 
4787  // conditionally decrement the CX register
4788  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr zero = operators()->number_(REG_anyCX.nBits(), 0);
4789  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr maybeDecrement = operators()->ite(in_loop, operators()->number_(REG_anyCX.nBits(), -1), zero);
4790  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr new_cx = operators()->add(readRegister(REG_anyCX), maybeDecrement);
4791  writeRegister(REG_anyCX, new_cx);
4792  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr nonzero_cx = operators()->invert(operators()->equalToZero(new_cx));
4793 
4794  // determine whether we should repeat the instruction.
4795  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr again;
4796  switch (repeat_prefix) {
4797  case x86_repeat_none:
4798  again = operators()->boolean_(false);
4799  break;
4800  case x86_repeat_repe:
4801  // REPE is an alias for REP when used with certain instructions.
4802  if (honorZeroFlag) {
4803  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr zf = readRegister(REG_ZF);
4804  again = operators()->and_(operators()->and_(in_loop, nonzero_cx), zf);
4805  } else {
4806  again = operators()->and_(in_loop, nonzero_cx);
4807  }
4808  break;
4809  case x86_repeat_repne: {
4810  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr notZf = operators()->invert(readRegister(REG_ZF));
4811  again = operators()->and_(operators()->and_(in_loop, nonzero_cx), notZf);
4812  break;
4813  }
4814  }
4815 
4816  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr ip = readRegister(REG_anyIP);
4817  writeRegister(REG_anyIP,
4818  operators()->ite(again,
4819  operators()->number_(REG_anyIP.nBits(), insn_va), // repeat
4820  ip)); // exit loop
4821 }
4822 
4823 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
4824 DispatcherX86::doAddOperation(BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr a, BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr b,
4825  bool invertCarries, const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &carryIn)
4826 {
4827  if (a->nBits() > b->nBits()) {
4828  b = operators()->signExtend(b, a->nBits());
4829  } else if (a->nBits() < b->nBits()) {
4830  a = operators()->signExtend(a, b->nBits());
4831  }
4832 
4833  ASSERT_require(1==carryIn->nBits());
4834  size_t nbits = a->nBits();
4835  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr carries;
4836  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr result = operators()->addWithCarries(a, b, invertMaybe(carryIn, invertCarries), carries/*out*/);
4837  setFlagsForResult(result);
4838  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr sign = operators()->extract(carries, nbits-1, nbits);
4839  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr ofbit = operators()->extract(carries, nbits-2, nbits-1);
4840  writeRegister(REG_AF, invertMaybe(operators()->extract(carries, 3, 4), invertCarries));
4841  writeRegister(REG_CF, invertMaybe(sign, invertCarries));
4842  writeRegister(REG_OF, operators()->xor_(sign, ofbit));
4843  return result;
4844 }
4845 
4846 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
4847 DispatcherX86::doAddOperation(BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr a, BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr b,
4848  bool invertCarries, const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &carryIn,
4849  const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &cond)
4850 {
4851  if (a->nBits() > b->nBits()) {
4852  b = operators()->signExtend(b, a->nBits());
4853  } else if (a->nBits() < b->nBits()) {
4854  a = operators()->signExtend(a, b->nBits());
4855  }
4856 
4857  ASSERT_require(1==carryIn->nBits());
4858  ASSERT_require(cond!=NULL && cond->nBits()==1);
4859  size_t nbits = a->nBits();
4860  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr carries;
4861  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr result = operators()->addWithCarries(a, b, invertMaybe(carryIn, invertCarries), carries/*out*/);
4862  setFlagsForResult(result, cond);
4863  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr sign = operators()->extract(carries, nbits-1, nbits);
4864  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr ofbit = operators()->extract(carries, nbits-2, nbits-1);
4865  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr af = readRegister(REG_AF);
4866  writeRegister(REG_AF,
4867  operators()->ite(cond,
4868  invertMaybe(operators()->extract(carries, 3, 4), invertCarries),
4869  af));
4870  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr cf = readRegister(REG_CF);
4871  writeRegister(REG_CF,
4872  operators()->ite(cond,
4873  invertMaybe(sign, invertCarries),
4874  cf));
4875  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr of = readRegister(REG_OF);
4876  writeRegister(REG_OF,
4877  operators()->ite(cond,
4878  operators()->xor_(sign, ofbit),
4879  of));
4880  return result;
4881 }

4883

4885 /* Does increment (decrement with DEC set), and adjusts condition flags. */
4886 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
4887 DispatcherX86::doIncOperation(const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &a, bool dec, bool setCarry)
4888 {
4889  size_t nbits = a->nBits();
4890  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr carries;
4891  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr no = operators()->boolean_(false);
4892  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr result = operators()->addWithCarries(a, number_(nbits, dec?-1:1), no, carries/*out*/);
4893  setFlagsForResult(result);
4894  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr sign = operators()->extract(carries, nbits-1, nbits);
4895  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr ofbit = operators()->extract(carries, nbits-2, nbits-1);
4896  writeRegister(REG_AF, invertMaybe(operators()->extract(carries, 3, 4), dec));
4897  writeRegister(REG_OF, operators()->xor_(sign, ofbit));
4898  if (setCarry)
4899  writeRegister(REG_CF, invertMaybe(sign, dec));
4900  return result;
4901 }
4902 
4903 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
4904 DispatcherX86::doRotateOperation(X86InstructionKind kind, const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &operand,
4905  const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &total_rotate, size_t rotateSignificantBits)
4906 {
4907  ASSERT_require(x86_rcl==kind || x86_rcr==kind || x86_rol==kind || x86_ror==kind);
4908  ASSERT_require(total_rotate->nBits()==8 && rotateSignificantBits<8);
4909 
4910  // The 8086 does not mask the rotate count; processors starting with the 80286 (including virtual-8086 mode) do mask. We
4911  // will always mask. The effect (other than timing) is the same either way.
4912  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr maskedRotateCount = operators()->extract(total_rotate, 0, rotateSignificantBits);
4913  if (operand->nBits()==9 || operand->nBits()==17) { // RCL or RCR on an 8- or 16-bit operand
4914  maskedRotateCount = operators()->unsignedModulo(maskedRotateCount,
4915  number_(maskedRotateCount->nBits(), operand->nBits()));
4916  }
4917  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr isZeroRotateCount = operators()->equalToZero(maskedRotateCount);
4918 
4919  // isOneBitRotate is true if the (masked) amount by which to rotate is equal to one.
4920  uintmax_t m = IntegerOps::genMask<uintmax_t>(rotateSignificantBits);
4921  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr mask = number_(rotateSignificantBits, m); // -1 in modulo arithmetic
4922  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr isOneBitRotate = operators()->equalToZero(operators()->add(maskedRotateCount, mask));
4923 
4924  // Do the actual rotate.
4925  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr result;
4926  switch (kind) {
4927  case x86_rcl:
4928  case x86_rol:
4929  result = operators()->rotateLeft(operand, maskedRotateCount);
4930  break;
4931  case x86_rcr:
4932  case x86_ror:
4933  result = operators()->rotateRight(operand, maskedRotateCount);
4934  break;
4935  default:
4936  ASSERT_not_reachable("instruction not handled");
4937  }
4938  ASSERT_require(result->nBits()==operand->nBits());
4939 
4940  // Compute the new CF value.
4941  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr new_cf;
4942  switch (kind) {
4943  case x86_rcl:
4944  case x86_rcr:
4945  case x86_ror:
4946  new_cf = operators()->extract(result, result->nBits()-1, result->nBits());
4947  break;
4948  case x86_rol:
4949  new_cf = operators()->extract(result, 0, 1);
4950  break;
4951  default:
4952  ASSERT_not_reachable("instruction not handled");
4953  }
4954 
4955  // Compute the new OF value. The new OF value is only used for 1-bit rotates.
4956  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr new_of;
4957  switch (kind) {
4958  case x86_rcl:
4959  case x86_ror: {
4960  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr v1 = operators()->extract(result, result->nBits()-2, result->nBits()-1);
4961  new_of = operators()->xor_(operators()->extract(result, result->nBits()-1, result->nBits()), v1);
4962  break;
4963  }
4964  case x86_rcr: {
4965  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr v1 = operators()->extract(operand, operand->nBits()-2, operand->nBits()-1);
4966  new_of = operators()->xor_(operators()->extract(operand, operand->nBits()-1, operand->nBits()), v1);
4967  break;
4968  }
4969  case x86_rol:
4970  new_of = operators()->xor_(new_cf,
4971  operators()->extract(result, result->nBits()-1, result->nBits()));
4972  break;
4973  default:
4974  ASSERT_not_reachable("instruction not handled");
4975  }
4976 
4977  // Update CF and OF flags. SF, ZF, AF, and PF are not affected.
4978  writeRegister(REG_CF, new_cf);
4979  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr maybeOf = operators()->ite(isOneBitRotate, new_of, unspecified_(1));
4980  writeRegister(REG_OF, operators()->ite(isZeroRotateCount,
4981  readRegister(REG_OF, PEEK_REGISTER),
4982  maybeOf));
4983 
4984  return result;
4985 }
4986 
4987 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
4988 DispatcherX86::doShiftOperation(X86InstructionKind kind, const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &operand,
4989  const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &source_bits, const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &total_shift,
4990  size_t shiftSignificantBits)
4991 {
4992  ASSERT_require(x86_shr==kind || x86_sar==kind || x86_shl==kind || x86_shld==kind || x86_shrd==kind);
4993  ASSERT_require(operand->nBits()==source_bits->nBits());
4994  ASSERT_require(total_shift->nBits()==8 && shiftSignificantBits<8);
4995 
4996  // The 8086 does not mask the shift count; processors starting with the 80286 (including virtual-8086 mode) do
4997  // mask. The effect (other than timing) is the same either way.
4998  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr maskedShiftCount = operators()->extract(total_shift, 0, shiftSignificantBits);
4999  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr isZeroShiftCount = operators()->equalToZero(maskedShiftCount);
5000 
5001  // isLargeShift is true if the (unmasked) amount by which to shift is greater than or equal to the size in
5002  // bits of the destination operand.
5003  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr extraShiftCount = operators()->extract(total_shift, shiftSignificantBits, 8);
5004  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr isLargeShift = operators()->invert(operators()->equalToZero(extraShiftCount));
5005 
5006  // isOneBitShift is true if the (masked) amount by which to shift is equal to one.
5007  uintmax_t m = IntegerOps::genMask<uintmax_t>(shiftSignificantBits);
5008  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr mask = number_(shiftSignificantBits, m); // -1 in modulo arithmetic
5009  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr isOneBitShift = operators()->equalToZero(operators()->add(maskedShiftCount, mask));
5010 
5011  // Do the actual shift, according to instruction kind.
5012  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr result;
5013  switch (kind) {
5014  case x86_shr:
5015  result = operators()->shiftRight(operand, maskedShiftCount);
5016  break;
5017  case x86_sar:
5018  result = operators()->shiftRightArithmetic(operand, maskedShiftCount);
5019  break;
5020  case x86_shl:
5021  result = operators()->shiftLeft(operand, maskedShiftCount);
5022  break;
5023  case x86_shrd: {
5024  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr v1 = operators()->shiftLeft(source_bits, operators()->negate(maskedShiftCount));
5025  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr v2 = operators()->ite(isZeroShiftCount,
5026  number_(operand->nBits(), 0),
5027  v1);
5028  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr v3 = operators()->or_(operators()->shiftRight(operand, maskedShiftCount), v2);
5029  result = operators()->ite(isLargeShift, unspecified_(operand->nBits()), v3);
5030  break;
5031  }
5032  case x86_shld: {
5033  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr v1 = operators()->shiftRight(source_bits, operators()->negate(maskedShiftCount));
5034  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr v2 = operators()->ite(isZeroShiftCount,
5035  number_(operand->nBits(), 0),
5036  v1);
5037  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr v3 = operators()->or_(operators()->shiftLeft(operand, maskedShiftCount), v2);
5038  result = operators()->ite(isLargeShift, unspecified_(operand->nBits()), v3);
5039  break;
5040  }
5041  default:
5042  ASSERT_not_reachable("instruction not handled");
5043  }
5044  ASSERT_require(operand->nBits()==result->nBits());
5045  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr originalSign = operators()->extract(operand, operand->nBits()-1, operand->nBits());
5046  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr resultSign = operators()->extract(result, result->nBits()-1, result->nBits());
5047 
5048  // The AF flag is undefined if a shift occurs. The documentation for SHL, SHR, and SAR are somewhat ambiguous about
5049  // this, but the documentation for SHLD and SHRD is more specific. We assume that both sets of shift instructions
5050  // behave the same way.
5051  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr unspecAf = unspecified_(1);
5052  writeRegister(REG_AF,
5053  operators()->ite(isZeroShiftCount,
5054  readRegister(REG_AF, PEEK_REGISTER),
5055  unspecAf));
5056 
5057  // What is the last bit shifted off the operand? If we're right shifting by N bits, then the original operand N-1 bit
5058  // is what should make it into the final CF; if we're left shifting by N bits then we need bit operand->nBits()-N.
5059  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr bitPosition;
5060  if (x86_shr==kind || x86_sar==kind || x86_shrd==kind) {
5061  bitPosition = operators()->add(maskedShiftCount, mask);
5062  } else {
5063  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr one = number_(shiftSignificantBits, 1);
5064  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr term1 = operators()->add(operators()->invert(maskedShiftCount), one);
5065  bitPosition = operators()->add(number_(shiftSignificantBits, operand->nBits() & m), // probably zero modulo
5066  term1);
5067  }
5068  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr shifted_off = operators()->extract(operators()->shiftRight(operand, bitPosition), 0, 1);
5069 
5070  // New carry flag value. From the Intel manual, the CF flag is "undefined for SHL and SHR [and SAL] instructions where
5071  // the count is greater than or equal to the size (in bits) of the destination operand", and "if the count is 0, the
5072  // flags are not affected." The manual is silent about the value of CF for large SAR shifts, so we use the original
5073  // sign bit, matching the pseudo-code in the manual.
5074  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr newCFite = operators()->ite(isLargeShift,
5075  (x86_sar==kind ? originalSign : unspecified_(1)),
5076  shifted_off);
5077  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr newCF = operators()->ite(isZeroShiftCount, readRegister(REG_CF, PEEK_REGISTER), newCFite);
5078  writeRegister(REG_CF, newCF);
5079 
5080  // Ajust the overflow flag. From the Intel manual for the SHL, SHR, and SAR instructions, "The OF flag is affected
5081  // only on 1-bit shifts. For left shifts, the OF flag is set to 0 if the most-significant bit of the result is the
5082  // same as the CF flag (that is, the top two bits of the original operand were the same); otherwise, it is set to 1.
5083  // For the SAR instruction, the OF flag is cleared for all 1-bit shifts. For the SHR instruction, the OF flag is set
5084  // to the most-significant bit of the original operand." Later, it states that "the OF flag is affected only for 1-bit
5085  // shifts; otherwise it is undefined." We're assuming that the statement "if the count is 0, then the flags are not
5086  // affected" takes precedence. For SHLD and SHRD it says, "for a 1-bit shift, the OF flag is set if a sign changed
5087  // occurred; otherwise it is cleared. For shifts greater than 1 bit, the OF flag is undefined."
5088  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr newOF;
5089  switch (kind) {
5090  case x86_shr: {
5091  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr unspec = unspecified_(1);
5092  newOF = operators()->ite(isOneBitShift,
5093  originalSign,
5094  operators()->ite(isZeroShiftCount,
5095  readRegister(REG_OF, PEEK_REGISTER),
5096  unspec));
5097  break;
5098  }
5099  case x86_sar: {
5100  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr unspec = unspecified_(1);
5101  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr v1 = operators()->ite(isZeroShiftCount, readRegister(REG_OF, PEEK_REGISTER), unspec);
5102  newOF = operators()->ite(isOneBitShift, operators()->boolean_(false), v1);
5103  break;
5104  }
5105  case x86_shl:
5106  case x86_shld:
5107  case x86_shrd: {
5108  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr unspec = unspecified_(1);
5109  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr v1 = operators()->ite(isZeroShiftCount, readRegister(REG_OF, PEEK_REGISTER), unspec);
5110  newOF = operators()->ite(isOneBitShift, operators()->xor_(originalSign, resultSign), v1);
5111  break;
5112  }
5113  default:
5114  ASSERT_not_reachable("instruction not handled");
5115  }
5116  writeRegister(REG_OF, newOF);
5117 
5118  // Result flags SF, ZF, and PF are set according to the result, but are unchanged if the shift count is zero.
5119  setFlagsForResult(result, operators()->invert(isZeroShiftCount));
5120  return result;
5121 }
5122 
5123 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
5124 DispatcherX86::readRegister(RegisterDescriptor reg, AccessMode mode) {
5125  // When reading FLAGS, EFLAGS as a whole do not coalesce individual flags into the single register.
5126  if (reg.majorNumber()==x86_regclass_flags && reg.offset()==0 && reg.nBits()>1) {
5127  if (BaseSemantics::State::Ptr ss = operators()->currentState()) {
5128  BaseSemantics::RegisterState::Ptr rs = ss->registerState();
5129  if (BaseSemantics::RegisterStateGeneric *rsg = dynamic_cast<BaseSemantics::RegisterStateGeneric*>(rs.get())) {
5130  BaseSemantics::RegisterStateGeneric::AccessModifiesExistingLocationsGuard guard(rsg, false);
5131  switch (mode) {
5132  case READ_REGISTER:
5133  return operators()->readRegister(reg);
5134  case PEEK_REGISTER:
5135  return operators()->peekRegister(reg, operators()->undefined_(reg.nBits()));
5136  }
5137  }
5138  }
5139  }
5140  switch (mode) {
5141  case READ_REGISTER:
5142  return operators()->readRegister(reg);
5143  case PEEK_REGISTER:
5144  return operators()->peekRegister(reg, operators()->undefined_(reg.nBits()));
5145  }
5146  ASSERT_not_reachable("unhandled access mode");
5147 }
5148 
5149 void
5150 DispatcherX86::writeRegister(RegisterDescriptor reg, const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &value) {
5151  if (reg.nBits() == 32 && reg.offset() == 0 && REG_anyIP.nBits() == 64) {
5152  // Writing to a 32-bit GPR in x86-64 will also clear the upper 32 bits of the same 64-bit register. E.g., "MOV EDI,
5153  // EDI" is one way to clear the upper 32-bits in RDI.
5154  if (reg.majorNumber() == x86_regclass_gpr || reg.majorNumber() == x86_regclass_ip) {
5155  RegisterDescriptor upperHalf(reg.majorNumber(), reg.minorNumber(), 32, 32);
5156  operators()->writeRegister(upperHalf, operators()->number_(32, 0));
5157  }
5158  } else if (reg.majorNumber()==x86_regclass_st && reg.minorNumber()<8 && reg.offset()==0 && reg.nBits()==64) {
5159  // When writing to an MM register, the high-order 16 bits are set in order to make the underlying
5160  // ST register NaN.
5161  RegisterDescriptor wider = reg;
5162  wider.nBits(80);
5163  operators()->writeRegister(wider, operators()->concat(value, number_(16, 0xffff)));
5164  return;
5165  }
5166  operators()->writeRegister(reg, value);
5167 }
5168 
5169 void
5170 DispatcherX86::write(SgAsmExpression *e, const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &value, size_t addr_nbits/*=0*/)

5179 void
5180 DispatcherX86::pushFloatingPoint(const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &value)
5181 {
5182  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr topOfStack = readRegister(REG_FPSTATUS_TOP);
5183  if (!topOfStack->isConcrete())
5184  throw BaseSemantics::NotImplemented("FP-stack top is not concrete", NULL);
5185  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr newTopOfStack = operators()->add(topOfStack, operators()->number_(topOfStack->nBits(), -1));
5186  ASSERT_require2(newTopOfStack->isConcrete(), "constant folding is required for FP-stack");
5187 
5188  RegisterDescriptor reg(REG_ST0.majorNumber(), (REG_ST0.minorNumber() + newTopOfStack->toUnsigned().get()) % 8,
5189  REG_ST0.offset(), REG_ST0.nBits());
5190  writeRegister(reg, value);
5191  writeRegister(REG_FPSTATUS_TOP, newTopOfStack);
5192 }

5194 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
5195 DispatcherX86::readFloatingPointStack(size_t /*position*/)

5199  throw BaseSemantics::NotImplemented("FP-stack top is not concrete", NULL);
5200  RegisterDescriptor reg(REG_ST0.majorNumber(), (REG_ST0.minorNumber() + topOfStack->toUnsigned().get()) % 8,
5201  REG_ST0.offset(), REG_ST0.nBits());
5202  return readRegister(reg);
5203 }

5206 DispatcherX86::popFloatingPoint()

5217 DispatcherX86::fixMemoryAddress(const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &addr) const
5218 {
5219  if (size_t addrWidth = addressWidth()) {
5220  if (addr->nBits() < addrWidth)
5221  return operators()->signExtend(addr, addrWidth);
5222  if (addr->nBits() > addrWidth)
5223  return operators()->unsignedExtend(addr, addrWidth);
5224  }
5225  return addr;
5226 }

5228 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
5229 DispatcherX86::saturateSignedToUnsigned(const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &src, size_t nBits) {
5230  ASSERT_not_null(src);
5231  ASSERT_require(src->nBits() >= nBits);
5232  if (src->nBits() == nBits)
5233  return src;
5234  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr signBit = operators()->extract(src, src->nBits()-1, src->nBits());
5235  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr high = operators()->extract(src, nBits, src->nBits());
5236  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr noOverflow = operators()->equalToZero(high);
5237  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr v1 = operators()->signExtend(signBit, nBits);
5238  return operators()->ite(noOverflow, operators()->extract(src, 0, nBits), v1);
5239 }
5240 
5241 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
5242 DispatcherX86::saturateSignedToSigned(const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &src, size_t nBits) {
5243  ASSERT_not_null(src);
5244  ASSERT_require(src->nBits() >= nBits);
5245  if (src->nBits() == nBits)
5246  return src;
5247  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr signBit = operators()->extract(src, src->nBits()-1, src->nBits());
5248  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr high = operators()->extract(src, nBits-1, src->nBits());
5249  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr zero = operators()->number_(high->nBits(), 0);
5250  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr allSet = operators()->invert(zero);
5251  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr highZerop = operators()->isEqual(high, allSet);
5252  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr noOverflow = operators()->or_(operators()->equalToZero(high), highZerop);
5253  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr yes = operators()->boolean_(true);
5254  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr minResult = operators()->concat(operators()->number_(nBits-1, 0), yes);
5255  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr maxResult = operators()->invert(minResult);
5256  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr minOrMax = operators()->ite(signBit, minResult, maxResult);
5257  return operators()->ite(noOverflow, operators()->extract(src, 0, nBits), minOrMax);
5258 }
5259 
5260 BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr
5261 DispatcherX86::saturateUnsignedToUnsigned(const BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr &src, size_t nBits) {
5262  ASSERT_not_null(src);
5263  ASSERT_require(src->nBits() >= nBits);
5264  if (src->nBits() == nBits)
5265  return src;
5266  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr high = operators()->extract(src, nBits, src->nBits());
5267  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr noOverflow = operators()->equalToZero(high);
5268  BaseSemantics::SValue::Ptr allBits = operators()->invert(operators()->number_(nBits, 0));
5269  return operators()->ite(noOverflow, operators()->extract(src, 0, nBits), allBits);
5270 }
